newsitem.title: UK: Sainsbury up in firm supermarket sector.
newsitem.headline: Sainsbury up in firm supermarket sector.

text.p: Shares in J. Sainsbury Plc rose in a firm food retail sector on Thursday, as the stock rebounded from recent extended weakness, traders and analysts said.

Some said food retailers could be attractive if inflation starts to pick up, yet despite today's higher-than-expected price data analysts said there was still little evidence of food prices gaining pace.
"I don't think there is any evidence of food price inflation in today's numbers," said one analyst.
Sainsbury was up 7p at 348-1/2 by 1049 GMT, after earlier this week dropping to its lowest level since January 1992.
Said one trader: "The whole sector is looking OK and Sainsbury is leading the charge." Another added: "We are seeing a few cheap buyers of Sainsbury and the sector is having a bit of a bounce."
Other food retailers were also firm in a generally weak market, with Tesco Plc up 1-1/2p at 325-1/2, ASDA Group Plc up 1/4 at 117-3/4 and Safeway Plc up 3p at 356.
